[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Fidelity Investments, the privately held mutual fund and financial services company headquartered in Boston, built a 200 million dollar data center in Papillion, Nebraska, near Omaha, first revealed publicly after operating under the code name Project Photon. Announced in October 2012 with construction beginning immediately and operational status targeted for 2014, the facility was expected to employ 30 to 35 people once complete and was designed to achieve LEED green building certification. Fidelity became the first company to use Nebraskas Tier 2 Plus-Large Data Center tax incentive provision, with then-governor Dave Heineman citing the project as a benchmark for other companies considering Nebraska data center locations. As with Fidelitys other data center investments, the Papillion facility exists to support the companys own internal financial services technology infrastructure, including trading systems, account management, and other mutual fund and brokerage operations, rather than functioning as a commercial colocation offering to outside tenants. Fidelitys privately held, member owned corporate structure means it does not file SEC disclosures on the scale of a publicly traded company, so facility-level detail in this registry relies on trade press coverage of the original 2012 announcement rather than ongoing operator disclosure. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
Fidelity operates a data center in Papillion, Nebraska that was built in 2012-2014 as a $200 million facility to support the company's internal financial services infrastructure, including trading systems and account management. The campus publishes no megawatt specification, so its IT load cannot be assessed against typical AI training densities.

Nebraska has 21 mapped data center facilities, but none publish power consumption figures, making this campus's scale relative to other sites in the state unknowable from available data. Fidelity designed the facility to achieve LEED certification and operates it exclusively for internal use rather than as a commercial colocation offering.

The absence of published power specifications means this campus cannot be ranked among facilities that matter to AI scaling as measured by this site's framework, which depends on documented compute capacity to assess grid constraints on AI deployment.
